text:
maya: Heads up — found a small but annoying discrepancy between the Python/TS SDKs and the REST handler that can flip booleans. Repro + short thread below.

maya: Context: POST /v1/embeddings. SDKs have an `includeMetadata` param (default false). Python omits the field when false; TS SDK sometimes emits it as the string 'false' in the JSON payload. Our legacy backend treats any present non-null value as truthy, so 'false' -> true for some downstream code paths.

maya: Repro commands:
```
# curl (works as expected, omits includeMetadata)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"hi"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'

# TS SDK (broken example output shows string)
// ts call
client.embeddings.create({ input: 'hi', includeMetadata: false })
// payload sent: { input: "hi", includeMetadata: "false" }

# Py SDK (ok)
client.embeddings.create(input='hi', include_metadata=False)
# payload: { input: "hi" }  # omitted
```

tom: Ugh. Thanks for the write-up. Which serializer in the TS SDK is responsible? FormData/json builder?

kevin: Likely the query-param/compact serializer we added for small payload optimization. It coalesces values via String(val) in one path — that's where booleans become strings.

sarah: I can take this in the TS SDK. Two options: (A) stop stringifying booleans and omit defaults, (B) explicitly coerce 'false'/'true' strings back to booleans in the server. Prefer fix in SDK but will do both short-term.

maya: Impact: some customers using server-side analyzers that check presence-of-field will get flipped semantics. Need quick mitigation in API gateway + SDK fix.

tom: Short-term server change: treat the strings 'true'/'false' as actual booleans; accept both `include_metadata` and `includeMetadata` names to avoid casing breakage. Long-term: SDKs should omit defaulted params.

sarah: Opening PR for ts-sdk right now. I'll add unit tests for serializer branch and a small e2e that asserts payload symmetry with Python SDK.

sarah: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/224 (WIP) — changes:
- don't call String() for boolean values in compact serializer
- omit keys equal to default values when omitDefaults config enabled
- add integration test comparing py/ts payloads

kevin: Nice. I'll add an integration test in runtime repo to assert the backend treats both representations the same.

maya: Quick server mitigation plan I pushed to staging: add a compatibility layer in request normalization that runs before the handler:
```
// pseudo
for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(body)) {
  if (typeof v === 'string' && (v === 'true' || v === 'false')) {
    body[k] = (v === 'true')
  }
}
// also accept include_metadata alias
if (body.includeMetadata && body.include_metadata === undefined) body.include_metadata = body.includeMetadata
```

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out compat patch to staging (service/runtime): 2026-03-17T15:42:00Z — config: normal canary 10%

maya: :thumbsup: Can we also add a short entry in the changelog / SDK migration notes? This is easy to miss by integrators.

tom: I'll add a migration note and flag this in the API contract doc (under parameter serialization gotchas).

sarah: FYI — I added a lint rule to ts-sdk to fail if someone calls String() on booleans in the serializer path. PR updated.

kevin: After CI, I'll run the new integration tests against canary staging. If green we promote the compat patch to prod and then cut the SDK release.

maya: Closing loop: once TS PR merged + runtime change promoted to prod + integration tests green, we announce in #product-announce? maybe just send a short note to customers who use the raw REST.

tom: Agreed — small targeted customer note + changelog.

maya: Thanks all. Leaving follow-ups:
- sasha -> merge + cut ts-sdk patch release (sarah)
- kevin -> integration test + promote runtime patch to prod if green
- tom -> add API doc note + changelog entry

maya: I'll check back tomorrow and mark resolved here.
